articles.title: Solheim Cup 2026: Who is playing for Team USA? Angela Stanford's line-up to face Team Europe and how they qualified
articles.summary: Who has qualified for Team USA and how did they do it? A closer look at Angela Stanford's Solheim Cup squad ahead of trying to regain the trophy against Team Europe; watch the Solheim Cup live from September 11-13 on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
Stanford has just two rookies in her line-up at Bernardus Golf from September 11-13, with the other 10 having played in at least one previous Solheim Cup and eight returning from their impressive 15.5-12.5 win on home soil two years ago.

Four-time major winner Nelly Korda is the headline name involved and topped the two-year qualification campaign, which ran from the 2024 FM Championship to the 2026 CPKC Women's Open last month.

The top seven players on the Solheim Cup points list at the end of the qualification campaign all earned automatic spots, with Korda joined by Angel Yin, Jennifer Kupcho, Yealimi Noh, Auston Kim, Lauren Coughlin and Allisen Corpuz.

Andrea Lee and Alison Lee automatically qualified as the next two available players in the Rolex Women's World Golf Rankings, before Lindy Duncan, Megan Khang, Rose Zhang took Stanford's three captain's picks.

We take a closer look at the American players chasing a first away win over Team Europe since 2015 and how they secured their spots…

Nelly Korda - US Solheim Cup points standings

Solheim Cup appearances: Four (2019, 2021, 2023, 2024)

Solheim Cup points: 10.5 points from 16 matches (10 wins, one tie, five losses)

Korda has been the dominant force in the women's game in recent seasons, with the world No 1 having her fifth consecutive Solheim Cup appearance wrapped up with months to spare after four wins during the first half of the year.

She has won at least two points from all of her previous four appearances, including an unbeaten debut at Gleneagles in 2019 and three points - before being thrashed by Charley Hull in the singles - during Team USA's win in 2024.

Angel Yin - US Solheim Cup points standings

Solheim Cup appearances: Three (2017, 2019, 2023)

Solheim Cup points: 5.5 points from nine matches (Five wins, one tie, three losses)

Yin was part of the joint-biggest fourballs win in Solheim Cup history when her and Ally Ewing beat Anna Nordqvist and Caroline Hedwall 7&5 in 2019, while she holds an unbeaten singles record against Team Europe.

The two-time LPGA Tour has qualified via the points list for the first time, having secured her spot via the world rankings in 2019 and a captain's pick the other appearances, although sat out of the final two months of the qualification campaign due to illness.

Jennifer Kupcho - US Solheim Cup points standings

Solheim Cup appearances: Three (2021, 2023, 2024)

Solheim Cup points: Four points from 10 matches (three wins, two tied, five losses)

Kupcho was joint-top scorer for Team USA on her debut in 2021, posting 2.5 points before being thrashed by Leona Maguire in the singles, then beat Linn Grant on the final day of Team USA's win in 2024.

She won the Shoprite LPGA Classic last June and added three top-10s in majors this season, including a share of eighth at the US Women's Open, with Kupcho now an automatic qualifier for a fourth consecutive Solheim Cup appearance.

Yealimi Noh - US Solheim Cup points standings

Solheim Cup points: Two points from three matches (two wins and one loss)

Noh returns after a five-year absence and faces a first Solheim Cup on European soil, having played in both fourballs sessions and defeated Mel Reid in the singles during Team USA's 2021 defeat.

She claimed her maiden LPGA Tour title at the 2025 Founders Cup and has four top-20 finishes in the majors during the two-year qualification campaign, including third at the AIG Women's Open.

Auston Kim - US Solheim Cup points standings

Kim was in her LPGA Tour rookie year during the last Solheim Cup but will debut for Team USA this time around, having enjoyed two consistent seasons during the qualification campaign.

She followed her runner-up finish at last year's KPMG Women's PGA Championship by earning second at the HSBC Women's World Championship earlier this year, where she then added two top-10s in majors to secure her automatic spot.

Lauren Coughlin - US Solheim Cup points standings

Solheim Cup points: 3.5 points from four matches (Three wins, one tie)

Coughlin returns for her second appearance after finishing undefeated in her 2024 debut, winning both foursomes matches and claiming victory with Sarah Schmelzel in fourballs before tying her Sunday singles clash with Maja Stark.

The three-time LPGA Tour winner also featured for Team USA at the Hanwha LIFEPLUS International Crown last year and won the Aramco Championship in April, with Coughlin finding form late in the summer.

Allisen Corpuz - US Solheim Cup points standings

Solheim Cup appearances: Two (2023, 2024)

Solheim Cup points: 5.5 points from eight matches (Five wins, one tie, two losses)

Corpuz secured her qualification via the points standings for the third consecutive Solheim Cup, having racked up two top-eight finishes in majors among six top-10s on the LPGA Tour this season.

Her and Nelly Korda have won all four foursomes matches together across the last two Solheim Cups, the joint-best foursomes record of any American pair in history, with Corpuz also despatching Anna Nordqvist in the singles two years ago.

Andrea Lee - Rolex Women's World Golf Rankings

Solheim Cup points: Four points from seven matches (Three wins, two ties, two losses)

Lee qualified via the points lists in the previous two Solheim Cups but gets in via world ranking this time, having led the fairways in regulation percentage on the LPGA Tour the last two seasons and posted 18 top-25 finishes.

She may well play alongside Zhang in the fourballs again in the Netherlands, having won their matches 5&4 and 6&4 when paired together in 2024. Lee also holds an unbeaten singles record, tying both her previous two matches in that format.

Alison Lee - Rolex Women's World Golf Rankings

Solheim Cup appearances: Two (2015, 2024)

Solheim Cup points: Two points from seven matches (Two wins, five losses)

Lee is the only member of Stanford's team to also be part of the last winning side on European soil in 2015, with this year's appearance her first for Team USA since becoming a mother last April.

She missed most of the qualification period on maternity leave but still picked up three top-five finishes in this season, including at the KPMG Women's PGA Championship. Lee becomes the first mum to compete for Team USA since Cristie Kerr in 2017.

Duncan held the second qualifying spot via the Rolex Women's World Golf Rankings for nearly two months before dropping out of position late in the qualification campaign, with the 35-year-old now the oldest debutant since Nancy Scranton in 2000.

She has amassed 14 top-25 finishes over the past two years, including a share of seventh at the HSBC Women's World Championship in March, although missed the cut in four of the five majors this season.

Solheim Cup points: 8.5 points from 13 matches (seven wins, three tied, three losses)

Khang had a disappointing finish to the qualification campaign but returns for a fifth consecutive Solheim Cup appearance, having ended unbeaten in each of the last two editions against Team Europe.

Since beating Sophia Povpov in the Sunday singles of their 2021 loss, Khang top-scored for Team USA two years later before winning all three of her matches in their 2024 victory.

Solheim Cup points: 4.5 points from seven matches (Four wins, one tie, two losses)

The two-time LPGA Tour winner heads into the Solheim Cup with top-eight finishes in her last two starts, lifting her back inside the world's top 50 after an inconsistent season.

Zhang played a star role in their 2024 victory, top-scoring for Team USA after winning all four of her matches with at least two holes to spare. Expect her dominant fourballs partnership with Andrea Lee to return in the Netherlands.

articles.title: DP World Tour: Paul Casey misses crucial putts at Omega European Masters as Thriston Lawrence claims third title
articles.summary: England's Paul Casey started the day six shots clear of Thriston Lawrence but was left to regret a series of missed putts; Watch the first round of the Amgen Irish Open live on Sky Sports Golf, with coverage starting on Thursday September 10 from 1.30pm
articles.body:
South Africa's Lawrence produced a stunning eight-under-par round at the to close a six-hole gap on Casey at the start of the day and force extra holes at Crans-sur-Sierre Golf Club in Switzerland.

Casey missed putts to win the tournament on the 18th hole in regulation play and then at each of the first three holes in the play-off and Lawrence made him pay with a brilliant birdie on the fourth extra hole to win this event for the third time.

"It's crazy. That's probably the most emotion I've ever shown, in a happy way. Normally I cry," he said.

"I can't believe it, but I just fought so hard today. I just gave it my everything."

Lawrence had led the tournament after two rounds, but a disappointing three-over-par 73 on Saturday saw him tumble six shots behind Casey.

However, he responded in brilliant fashion on Sunday, posting eight birdies in a blemish-free round to set the clubhouse target at 18 under.

Casey struggled on the front nine, recording bogeys on the par-three third and eighth holes on top of a double bogey at the sixth when he sent his second shot out of bounds.

However, he responded with his third birdie of the day on the ninth and added four more in the next six holes to move one shot clear of Lawrence with three holes to play.

He saved par with a fine putt on the 16th, but there was drama on the final hole when his second shot out of the rough remarkably bounced over the water and just shy of the green.

However, a difficult lie left him with a 20-foot putt for victory which he agonisingly missed to leave him two under par for the round and facing the play-off against Lawrence.

The two players produced pars at each of the first three extra holes, though Casey will particularly regret missing a 10ft birdie putt at the second and an eight-foot opportunity at the third.

The 49-year-old Englishman was seeking to win his first DP World Tour event in five and a half years, but after his birdie putt on the fourth play-off hole came up well short, Lawrence punished him and he collected his third red jacket from supermodel Cindy Crawford.

"He played great golf and it looked like it was his all day. Even in the play-off, he missed a couple of short ones.

"But it's just the best feeling in the world."

England's Harry Hall posted a seven-under-par final round to claim solo third place, one shot behind Lawrence and Casey.

Five players shared fourth a shot further back including the Spanish trio Angel Hildagao, Angel Ayora and Eugenio Chacarra plus Italy's Francesco Laporta and Austria's Bernd Wiesberger.

England's Matt Wallace (-15) shared ninth place, while Patrick Reed was a shot further back in a share of 11th.

articles.title: Solheim Cup 2026: Who is playing for Team Europe? Anna Nordqvist's line-up to face Team USA and how they qualified
articles.summary: Who has qualified for Team Europe and how did they do it? A closer look at Anna Nordqvist's Solheim Cup squad ahead of trying to regain the trophy against Team USA; watch the Solheim Cup live from September 11-13 on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
Nordqvist will have eight past Solheim Cup players in her team at Bernardus Golf from September 11-13, with four rookies - including world No 5 Lottie Woad - then completing the European line-up.

The qualification campaign ended after the AIG Women's Open on August 2, where Esther Henseleit's runner-up finish saw her join Charley Hull in qualifying via the LET Solheim Cup points list.

Woad, Maja Stark, Linn Grant, Celine Boutier, Carlota Ciganda and Nanna Koerstz Madsen secured their spots as the next six available players via the Rolex Women's World Golf Rankings, with Nordqvist announcing her four captain's picks a day later.

Ireland's Leona Maguire was handed a fourth consecutive Solheim Cup appearance, with Julia López Ramirez, Nastasia Nadaud and Mimi Rhodes all named as debutants to face Angela Stanford's side.

We take a closer look at the European players chasing home victory over Team USA and how they secured their spots…

Charley Hull (England) - LET Solheim Cup Points List

Solheim Cup appearances: Seven (2013, 2015, 2017, 2019, 2021, 2023, 2024)

Solheim Cup points: 16.5 points from 27 matches (15 wins, three ties, nine losses)

Hull won twice during the qualification campaign, including the PIF Saudi Ladies International in February, before going on to finish tied-second at the US Women's Open and tied-sixth at the AIG Women's Open.

She brings bags of experience and plenty of fire to Nordqvist's team, with the power-hitter Europe's top scorer in the 2024 Solheim Cup loss that included a 6&4 thrashing of Nelly Korda.

Esther Henseleit (Germany) - LET Solheim Cup Points List

Solheim Cup points: 1.5 points from three matches (one win, one tie and one loss)

Henseleit burst into form at the right time, finishing fourth at the ISPS HANDA Women's Scottish Open before an incredible final-hole birdie at the AIG Women's Open forced a play-off and lifted her into the second automatic spot on the LET points list.

Her debut at the Solheim Cup came in 2024, where she tied with Andrea Lee during the final-day singles after partnering Hull to one win and one loss in the foursomes over the first two days.

Lottie Woad (England) - Rolex Women's Golf World Rankings

Woad is already the highest-ranked European in the world rankings after picking up two LPGA Tour titles in her first year as a pro, having followed her ISPS Handa Women's Scottish Open win last July by winning the Kroger Queen City Championship in May.

She narrowly lost out in a play-off to Miyu Yamashita at the Meijer LPGA Classic and contended again at the AIG Women's Open, posting a third straight top-10 finish at that major. Can she follow her 2024 Curtis Cup glory by being part of more team success?

Maja Stark (Sweden) - Rolex Women's Golf World Rankings

Solheim Cup appearances: Two (2023, 2024)

Solheim Cup points: Four points from eight matches (won three, tied two, lost three)

The 2025 US Women's Open champion returns for her third Solheim Cup and comes into this event off the back of a strong major season, posting top-10 finishes at the US Women's Open and the Amundi Evian Championship.

Stark enjoyed a great debut in 2023, defeating then US Women's Open champion Allisen Corpuz in the singles to help Europe retain the Solheim Cup, then played three sessions with Emily Kristine Pedersen during the 2024 loss.

Celine Boutier (France) - Rolex Women's Golf World Rankings

Solheim Cup appearances: Four (2019, 2021, 2023, 2024)

Solheim Cup points: 7.5 points from 14 matches (won seven, tied one, lost six)

The Frenchwoman is one of only two Europeans to have won the LPGA Tour this season, claiming a one-shot win at the Shoprite LPGA Classic in May, then failing to contend in the next three majors before sharing 12th place at the AIG Women's Open.

Boutier won all four matches alongside Georgia Hall on debut during the 2019 victory and claimed a key point in the 2021 singles, with the former major champion losing all three matches in 2023 but returning two points in the most recent edition.

Carlota Ciganda - Rolex Women's Golf World Rankings

Solheim Cup points: 14 points from 27 matches (won 12, tied four, lost 11)

Ciganda experienced a dramatic drop in form after a strong 2025 and positive start to the season, missing the cut in the last four majors, although she offers plenty of Solheim Cup experience.

The Spaniard has been an ever-present member of the European squad since her 2013 debut, winning all four matches in the 2023 edition - including against Korda in the singles - to help Europe retain the trophy in dramatic fashion.

Linn Grant (Sweden) - Rolex Women's Golf World Rankings

Solheim Cup record: Three points from nine matches (three wins and six losses)

The Swede has struggled with form and fitness issues during a disappointing LPGA Tour campaign, missing the cut in the first three majors, but she returns for a third consecutive Solheim Cup appearance.

Grant formed an unbeaten fourballs partnership with Ciganda and led Europe out in the singles during the 2023 contest, but she was winless from four matches a year later.

Nanna Koerstz Madsen (Denmark) - Rolex Women's Golf World Rankings

Solheim Cup record: 1.5 points from 3 matches (one win, one tied, one loss)

Koerstz Madsen returns after a five-year absence, with the Dane initially looking set to rely on a captain's pick until Henseleit's qualification via the LET Solheim Cup points list secured her the final automatic spot from the world rankings.

She claimed a key final-hole fourball win alongside Ciganda during day two of the 2021 contest, helping Europe lead going into the final day, then tied with Austin Ernst in the singles of a historic away victory.

Leona Maguire (Ireland) - Captain's pick

Solheim Cup appearances: Three (2021, 2023, 2024)

Solheim Cup record: 8.5 points from 12 matches (eight wins, one tied, three losses)

Maguire has had to rely on a captain's pick after an inconsistent LPGA Tour season, during which a runner-up finish at the Aramco Championship in April and a tied-eighth at the last month's ISPS Handa Women's Scottish Open were the limited highlights.

She top-scored as an unbeaten rookie and played a star role in the 2021 win, and then played in every session during the following edition. She was, though, left frustrated by her limited involvement - playing just two sessions - during the 2024 defeat.

Julia Lopez Ramirez (Spain) - Captain's pick

The former amateur world No 1 has made a steady start to her professional career, enjoying a successful rookie season on the LPGA Tour last year and securing her Ladies European Tour status at Q-school later that season.

The big-hitting Spaniard has five top-25 finishes on the LPGA Tour in 2026, including at the ISPS Handa Women's Scottish Open, and her rookie appearance was confirmed after making the cut at the AIG Women's Open.

Nastasia Nadaud (France) - Captain's pick

Naduad won the LET's season-ending Andalucia Costa Del Sol Open de Espana in November, having already posted two runner-up finishes that campaign, before making a smooth transition onto the LPGA Tour.

Nordqvist described Nadaud as a player "who has been getting better and better", with the Frenchwoman making the cut in all five majors this season and still in contention to qualify for the LPGA Tour's CME Group Tour Championship.

Rhodes won the LET's Rookie of the Year title last season after claiming three victories in a breakout year - the Ford Women's New South Wales Open, the Joburg Ladies Open and the Dutch Ladies Open.

The Englishwoman has experience of featuring on a winning Curtis Cup team but now gets the chance to represent Team Europe. She was the last pick after a mixed debut season on the LPGA Tour.

articles.title: Green Party deputy leader Mothin Ali linked to property lets in Leeds
articles.summary: Mothin Ali, is linked to two rental properties via his company, but does not appear to profit from them.
articles.body:
The deputy leader of the Green Party, Mothin Ali, is linked to two buy-to-let properties, despite his party's opposition to private landlords.

Ali is the sole director of a company, which he set up and controls, that owns two rental properties in Leeds, bought in June 2022 and March 2025 - although he does not appear to profit from either of them.

The property purchases happened before the Greens adopted a policy committing to phasing out ownership of rental properties by private landlords in October 2025.

The Green Party told the BBC that, at the time Ali had set up the company, and since, he "has acted solely in the interests of vulnerable close family members for whom he has caring responsibilities".

Ali's connection to the rental properties via real estate company MA Holdings, which purchased them with buy-to-let mortgages, was first reported by the Times newspaper.

Records held by Companies House show that Ali is the sole director of MA Holdings, incorporated in December 2021, and he is listed in the records as the sole person with significant control, owning more than 75% of the shares.

The company's business includes "buying and selling of own real estate", "letting and operating of own or leased real estate" and "management of real estate on a fee or contract basis".

The BBC has spoken to the previous owner and resident of the second property, who confirmed that Ali's company had purchased the property and believed it was bought with the intention to be let out.

Asked why MA Holdings owns the rental properties, a Green Party spokesperson said: "We have provided deeply personal information to the BBC in confidence which shows that Councillor Ali has acted solely in the interests of vulnerable close family members for whom he has caring responsibilities.

"At Councillor Ali's request, we are not going to make this information public to protect his family."

The BBC is not publicising the personal information shared with it, at the request of the Greens, as it relates to private family matters.

In October last year, delegates to the Green Party's annual conference, passed a motion titled "Abolish landlords" , headed "the private rental sector has failed, it is a vehicle for wealth extraction, funnelling money from renters to the landlord class".

The motion states: "The effective abolition of private landlordism and the private rented sector, coupled with the mass expansion of council housing, is the only way to end the housing crisis."

This is now official policy for the Green Party of England and Wales, with a plan to increase regulation and taxes on private rentals to make it difficult for landlords to make a profit, while boosting housebuilding by councils.

The policy would use existing Green policies such as imposing rent controls, ending buy-to-let mortgages and giving councils the right to buy a rental property when it is sold at a discounted price.

Asked whether Ali had sought to take any steps since the policy had been adopted to change anything with regard to the rental properties, a Green Party spokesperson told the BBC he fully supported the policy.

"The policy does not literally seek to abolish landlords, but rather to put in more regulations and taxes on private rentals through measures such as rent controls and expanded social housing," they said. "All of which Mothin Ali supports."

When the policy was introduced, Green Party MP Carla Denyer told the BBC "while the motion to conference had an eye-catching name, it does not actually 'abolish' landlords".

"It does, however, address the housing crisis, empowers tenants and improves their wellbeing," she added.

"It contains a range of policies which, over time, would reduce the proportion of the housing market that is privately rented, and increase the proportion of socially rented homes."

articles.title: In 2015, Mark Pentecost paid $14.5 million for a 104-acre Florida island; after pouring millions into upgrades, it is asking $89 million with a 9-hole golf course and 29 developable lots
articles.summary: Real Estate News: Eleven years after buying a private retreat off Florida’s west coast for $14.5 million, entrepreneur Mark Pentecost has listed the 104-acre property f.
articles.body: Eleven years after buying a private retreat off Florida’s west coast for $14.5 million, entrepreneur Mark Pentecost has listed the 104-acre property for $89 million after spending millions on its transformation. The estate, historically known as Little Bokeelia Island, was listed through Coldwell Banker Realty and featured in Realtor.com's round-up of high-value American homes. The sharp rise in its value follows major improvements, including a private nine-hole golf course, upgraded infrastructure and 29 developable residential lots.From classroom teacher to island ownerPentecost, a former high-school mathematics teacher and basketball coach, made his fortune after founding the multi-level marketing company It Works! in 2001. The health and beauty business grew into a company worth hundreds of millions of dollars, allowing Pentecost and his wife, Cindy, to buy the island in July 2015. The couple paid much less than the property's original asking price of $29.5 million. At the time, the sale was recorded as one of the most expensive residential property deals in South-West Florida. Speaking shortly after the purchase, Pentecost described his vision for the private retreat. “Little Bokeelia is a slice of paradise that allows you to enjoy friendship, fun, freedom and to unplug from the chaos of today,” Mark Pentecost said in a statement released at the time. “It's in these moments when you're able to relax that you can brainstorm and innovate.”Historical roots and modern upgradesLocated in Pine Island Sound between Sarasota and Naples, the island has a history dating back to the early 20th century. Industrialist and dry-cell battery inventor Charles Frederick Burgess bought the property in 1924 and built a Spanish-style villa in 1928. He hosted notable guests there, including inventor Thomas Edison. During his 10 years of ownership, Pentecost transformed the island into a fully equipped corporate retreat and family compound. The estate is centred around the restored 1920s Addison Mizner-style main mansion, along with four guest cottages, a clubhouse, a caretaker's home and several recreational facilities. Together, the buildings contain 11 bedrooms, 10 full bathrooms and three half-baths. Along with the new nine-hole golf course, the property now has a pickleball court, full tennis and basketball courts, four deep-water docks, a resort-style swimming pool and a commercial-grade helipad for travel to and from the mainland. Property records from listing brokerages Coldwell Banker Realty and SWFLMLS show that the estate covers 104 acres with a large amount of shoreline. The 29 subdivided, developable lots could allow a future owner to turn the private island into an exclusive residential community or keep it as one large estate.Market positioningWith an asking price of $89 million, Little Bokeelia Island is now among the most expensive private island properties listed in the United States. Property records show annual taxes of about $115,166. Although the island is secluded and can only be reached by helicopter or boat, it is close to deep-water tarpon fishing and coastal areas near the historic Gasparilla Inn on nearby Boca Grande. Coldwell Banker and Pentecost's representatives have not publicly said whether the property will be sold as one unplatted parcel or whether developers will be able to buy individual subdivided lots. articles.title: Why potluck parties are making a big comeback in America
articles.summary: As Americans spend less time socialising, communities are rediscovering an old way of bringing people together.
articles.body:
Trenton, New Jersey — Long tables covered with American-flag tablecloths stand ready in the summer heat, as red, white and blue balloons sway overhead. The few dishes that have arrived are tucked under white mesh covers, while two grills sit at the edge of a driveway across the street.

Small American flags line the path to this grassy area beside a canal and a patch of trees. The trail begins at a large, dark burgundy sign that reads, “Welcome to Hiltonia, founded circa 1920”. The quiet neighbourhood of about 300 single-family homes, well-kept lawns and tree-lined streets is part of Trenton, New Jersey.

Only a handful of residents are mingling as Rich Green and Julie Kroon, a young couple in matching blue T-shirts, arrive with a bowl of corn and bean salad. Soon, others show up, greeting one another enthusiastically as they compliment the festive outfits and ask what everyone has brought to eat. As some struggle to open their folding chairs, others step in to help.

Thomas Emerick, a Hiltonia resident for 26 years, stands near the food table. Wearing a red-and-white striped shirt, he points to his contribution: a Thai black bean salad flavoured with garlic, ginger, cilantro and lime juice.

“You know what? You can have a social event without food, and you know how many people are going to come?” he asked. “Exactly. Now, if you feed them, they will come.”

Hiltonia’s gathering was part of America’s Potluck, a nationwide initiative led by the America250 Utah Commission to mark the country’s 250th anniversary through shared meals. But it also reflected a broader effort to rebuild social ties through one of the oldest social rituals: eating together. As loneliness and social divisions grow in the United States, communities, nonprofits and governments are turning to potlucks, communal dinners and other food-based gatherings to create opportunities for connection. Experts say these meals can bring neighbours to the same table, but lasting relationships depend on what happens after the dishes are cleared.

The July 5 America’s Potluck initiative encouraged people in every state to host or attend a potluck, with communities in all 50 states participating . While organisers had intended it to be a one-off event, they said some hosts are already preparing to do it again next year. Hiltonia was one of more than 1,700 such potlucks that took place across the country.

Dressed in a red sleeveless dress and sunglasses, Lily Knezevich, president of the Hiltonia Association, greeted everyone and made sure things were running smoothly at the event. A Hiltonia resident for more than 20 years, Knezevich learned about America’s Potluck through her involvement with Revolution NJ, New Jersey's initiative for organising semiquincentennial events.

The Hiltonia Association tries to keep people engaged with one another and encourages neighbours to support and look out for each other, Knezevich explained. Food is one way to make this happen.

“People naturally like to get together around food,” she said. “It's a great draw.”

Getting people to a table, of course, is the easy part. The tougher question is whether a meal can turn strangers into neighbours and friends — and whether a few hours of togetherness can build lasting connections. Research cannot yet tell us how long those relationships last, but it is beginning to shed light on the social benefits of eating together.

articles.title: European Masters: Thriston Lawrence beats Paul Casey on fourth play-off hole
articles.summary: England's Paul Casey is beaten by South Africa's defending champion Thriston Lawrence on the fourth play-off hole at the European Masters in Switzerland.
articles.body:
18 P Casey (Eng), T Lawrence*; -17 H Hall; -16 F Laporta (Ita), A Ayora (Spa), A Hidalgo (Spa), B Wiesberger (Aut), E Lopez-Chacarra (Spa)

Selected others : -15 M Wallace (Eng); -14 R Hoejgaard (Den), P Reed (US); -13 T Clements (Eng); -11 M Penge (Eng); -9 C Hill (Sco), S Garcia (Spa)

Paul Casey was beaten by South Africa's defending champion Thriston Lawrence on the fourth play-off hole at the European Masters in Switzerland.

The tournament was played at the Crans-sur-Sierre Golf Club in Crans-Montana, and Casey had pledged to donate his entire winnings to the victims of the New Year's Eve fire that killed 40 people in the Swiss mountain resort.

The 49-year-old Englishman missed four putts for the first prize of $637,500 (£469,112) - the first on his final hole in regulation and the next three on the first three play-off holes.

But after firing his approach to the back edge of the green at the fourth play-off hole, the former Ryder Cup player missed a chip and Lawrence sank his birdie putt to win the tournament for the third time - equalling the record of Seve Ballesteros.

Casey fired a two-under-par 68 in his final round to finish level on 18 under, with Lawrence forcing a play-off thanks to a stunning 62.

The LIV player was aiming for his 16th win on the DP World Tour and first since he claimed the Dubai Desert Classic in January 2021, but after finishing just short will now donate the runners-up prize of $412,500 (£303,543) to the Fondation Beloved , external .

England's Harry Hall finished third on 17 under after his closing 63.

Swiss regions ban pyrotechnics after ski bar fire

Casey secures Dubai Desert Classic title

"It's probably the most emotion I have ever shown in a happy way," said Lawrence, who hit eight birdies in a bogey-free round to set the clubhouse lead on 18 under.

"I fought so hard and just gave it my everything. I feel for Paul, he played great golf and it looked like it was his all day, even in the play-off. He missed a couple of short ones, but it's just the best feeling in the world."

Casey started the day six shots ahead of Lawrence, but struggled to rekindle the form that saw him hit 64 and 63 in his second and third rounds.

The LIV golfer dropped shots on three of his opening eight holes, including a double bogey six on the sixth.

Casey was two over for the day after a bogey on the eighth, but then picked up five birdies in the next seven holes to reclaim the lead.

The world number 707 made it up and down from a greenside bunker to save par on the 16th, then narrowly missed another birdie putt on the 17th to leave himself needing a par on the last for victory.

But he was unable to navigate the par four 18th safely after finding thick rough from the tee. Casey bounced his approach off a rock and over a stream into the rough guarding the green and after a poor chip shot missed a 20-foot putt for victory.

The difficult 18th hole was chosen for the play-off.

Both golfers made pars in their first two attempts, with Casey missing a 10-foot birdie putt to win on the second play-off hole.

Tournament organisers changed the pin position for the third play-off hole in an attempt to separate the two, but again they both made pars, with Casey seeing his eight-foot putt for the championship hit the cup and roll out.

And Lawrence finally punished his opponent on the fourth play-off hole.

articles.title: Walker Cup: Great Britain and Ireland make history with comeback win
articles.summary: Great Britain and Ireland produce the biggest comeback in Walker Cup history to defeat the United States and lift the trophy for the first time since 2015.
articles.body:
Great Britain and Ireland produced the biggest comeback in Walker Cup history to defeat the United States and lift the trophy for the first time since 2015.

At Lahinch in Ireland, the USA looked to be on the brink when they swept the morning foursomes to move just three-and-a-half points away from a sixth consecutive victory.

But GB&I picked up seven of the 10 points in the singles to clinch victory by 13-and-a-half points to 12-and-a-half and win for the first time in 11 years.

Josh Hill had the winning moment as he defeated world number two Tyler Watts on the final hole of the eighth pairing, and that sparked wild celebrations to mark a victory that seemed so unlikely after Sunday morning.

For Irish player Stuart Grehan, winning the biennial amateur tournament on home turf meant event more.

"I'm close to crying and I'm not an emotional person," Grehan told BBC Sport.

"It's unbelievable, it's the best feeling I've ever had on a golf course by a long stretch."

Grehan twice defeated world number one Preston Stout in the week, including in Sunday's decisive singles, and he said it was "incredible" to lead the fightback.

"With the way the day flowed, everyone on this team is just unbelievable," Grehan added.

"It's been an amazing week and to play Preston twice in the singles and get the better of him, I'm really proud of myself and it's amazing."

For captain Dean Robertson, the emotions were flowing as he guided GB&I to the Walker Cup for the 10th time.

"It's been very emotional and I could not be more proud," he said.

"I had full belief in the players, even at lunchtime when we went down 4-0."

After Grehan defeated Stout, who battled a bug in the lead-up to the event, in the opening match, that set the tone for the comeback that was to follow.

Luke Poulter - son of Ryder Cup legend Ian - delivered a moment of his own to beat Ethan Fang, before US Amateur champion Jack Whaley and star player Tyler Weaver also won their matches for the hosts.

Whaley's win, in particular, was impressive as he beat William Jennings by 8&7 - the biggest winning margin ever for a GB&I player.

Eliot Baker beat Stewart Hagestad on the final hole to claim his match, and Conor Graham won the last two holes to halve his match with Miles Russell before Hill's decisive moment came in a tight match up with Watts.

Even though Ryder Cowan and Josiah Gilbert defeated Ben Bolton and Sam Easterbrook, it came in the ninth and 10th pairings and the comeback was already completed as GB&I won by a single point.

When Hill was in the bunker on the 18th, captain Robertson said he thought of his late father and said the shot to get onto the green was reminiscent of Matthew Fitzpatrick's famous bunker shot to help earn his brother, Alex, a tour card at the Zurich Classic in April.

"I felt quite calm when Josh was hitting his putt and my thoughts were with my late dad," Scot Robertson added.

"To have my mum, brother and all my family here is really special and it's been a really emotional day."

articles.title: Walker Cup: Great Britain and Ireland produce stunning late comeback to beat USA 13½-12½ in thrilling contest
articles.summary: USA missed four putts to retain the trophy after whitewashing Great Britain and Ireland in the morning foursomes; Watch the first round of the Amgen Irish Open live on Sky Sports Golf, with coverage starting on Thursday September 10 from 1:30pm
articles.body:
Dean Robertson's side looked to be heading for defeat at Lahinch after suffering a clean sweep of defeats in the Sunday morning foursomes and with the Americans three points ahead going into the singles matches.

But the home side lost only two of the 10 matches and the competition eventually came down to the very last as Josh Hill won the 18th hole of his match with Tyler Watts to seal an incredible victory.

The USA will be left to regret the late turnaround after four missed putts to retain the Walker Cup.

Team GB&I needed a quick start to produce any sort of comeback and they delivered after Stuart Grehan, Luke Poulter - son of former Ryder Cup star Ian - Jack Whaley and Tyler Weaver all won their matches.

However, the Americans steadied the ship after securing halves through Miles Russell and Kihei Akina and wins courtesy of Ryder Cowan and Josiah Gilbert as it looked like they had thwarted the comeback.

As it looked like the Americans were about to take a firm grip on yet another win, Team GB&I responded once again. Eliot Baker overcame Stewart Hagestad on the final hole to ensure the Walker Cup would be determined on the final hole.

Hill and Tyler Watts were all square coming down the last at County Clare and Hill produced a stunning up-and-down from the bunker to complete a thrilling comeback and seal the unlikeliest of wins.

Speaking after securing the decisive point, Hill said: "This is absolutely unbelievable. It doesn't get better than this."

Captain Robertson added: "We are so elated. We're hardly able to put it into words. There's a lot of emotion, a lot of happy tears. But pride is the word I would use to describe this.

"There was most definitely a belief in the players and even though we were swept 4-0 this morning, there wasn't a despondency.

"The boys have delivered and I am incredibly proud of each and every one of them."

The victory by GB&I ends the streak of five victories in the Walker Cup by the USA and is their 10th win overall.

USA captain Nathan Smith refused to criticise his players, saying: "The match was incredible. It was definitely a tale of two days with what happened this morning and going forward now and how they played this afternoon.

"We knew how great their team was. They're a great team. They're a deep team. We knew they were capable of anything. Really at no time did we take the foot off the accelerator.

"All you can do is really tip your cap to them. They played great."

The morning session saw GB&I lose all the momentum they'd claimed on Sunday as the USA comprehensively won all four matches to move into a three-point lead.

Home captain Robertson stuck with his pairings from Saturday, but his players struggled to perform and failed to take the lead in any of the four matches.

The demise started as Grehan and Baker were beaten 3&2 in the opening match of the day by Stout and Fang.

Leng Jr. and Akina took out Poulter and Easterbrook by 4&3 in the second match, while Russell and Watts had little trouble in overcoming Weaver and Graham 3&2.

In the final match, the USA duo of Jennings and Cowan took the lead against Sheils Donegan and Hill on the second hole and never looked back, taking a 4&3 victory to leave the visitors needing just 3½ points in the afternoon session.

articles.title: Vishesh Sharma fights off tough conditions to win Golconda Masters on home course
articles.summary: Golf News: NEW DELHI: Two days after lifting the Golconda Masters trophy at the Hyderabad Golf Association (HGA), 19-year old Vishesh Sharma reflected on a victo.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Two days after lifting the Golconda Masters trophy at the Hyderabad Golf Association (HGA), 19-year old Vishesh Sharma reflected on a victory that was shaped by home support, demanding course conditions and the realities of pursuing professional golf in India as a self-funded athlete.The Golconda Masters is one of the marquee events on the PGTI calendar. Vishesh’s consistency across changing conditions proved decisive as he emerged on top in a tightly contested field.“The greens were phenomenal and rolling at great speeds. The rough was up as usual, so it’s always quite a challenge around the greens,” Vishesh said. “The showers made the course play differently almost every day, so all of us had to adapt and strategise accordingly.”Although familiar with HGA, he believes the biggest advantage came not from local knowledge but from the people walking alongside him.“What was special for me this week was having my friends, family and my coach there supporting me throughout. I think that was one of the key things that helped me secure this win,” he said.The title is another significant step in the 19-year-old’s steady rise on the PGTI, but his journey has been far from glamorous. Vishesh funds his own career, managing travel and equipment.His introduction to golf was almost accidental. Growing up in Vadodara, where his father worked as a govt officer, the family took a membership at the Gaekwad Baroda Golf Club primarily for recreational activities.“We used to go there for swimming, tennis and other activities. Golf happened coincidentally. I started going to the course, played a couple of junior events and gradually got into the sport,” he recalled.That gradual progression has also shaped his perspective on success and failure. “I wouldn’t say there’s one particular week because in golf, every week teaches us something. Whether it’s a win or whether we miss the cut, we learn more about ourselves and how we can get better,” he said.The standard of Indian golf has risen noticeably this season, with stronger fields and increased prize purses following the DP World Tour’s partnership with the PGTI. “DP World being our umbrella partner doesn’t just help financially. The name itself carries a certain weight and gives players confidence to go out there and show that we can compete,” he said.Even with constant travel across the country, his preparation remains remarkably consistent. Together with his coach, Vishesh follows a structured practice routine before every event, modifying only the finer details to suit each venue.With the Golconda Masters title secured, Vishesh has reinforced his place among PGTI’s in-form golfers while underlining the determination required to succeed in a demanding individual sport.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Packers Former 6th-Round Pick Lands $22M Extension
articles.summary: Former Green Bay Packers sixth-round draft pick Jon Runyan Jr. signed a two-year, $22M extension. With $21.5M in guaranteed salary, the deal will ensure he i...
articles.body:
Former Green Bay Packers sixth-round draft pick Jon Runyan Jr. signed a two-year, $22M extension. With $21.5M in guaranteed salary, the deal will ensure he is on the team for the next two seasons.

Runyan signed with the Giants in 2024, so by the time his extension is up, he will have spent four years with the Packers and four years with the Giants.

Former Green Bay Packers Offensive Lineman Jon Runyan Jr. Signs Extension With New York Giants

The son of a long-time NFL player, Runyan fell in the draft due to his lack of physical traits. However, the 192nd overall pick in the 2020 NFL Draft now has 79 career starts and is set to start in Week 1 for the Giants.

He did not start at all in his rookie season. However, he started the next three seasons in Green Bay. In 2021, he started at left guard. In 2022, it was a mix of left and right guard. Then, in 2023, he started at right guard.

So, he signed a three-year, $30M deal with the Giants in free agency. He started at left guard for the Giants for the next two seasons. So, entering the last year of his deal, he saw a small increase in pay and got a two-year extension.

This is notable considering the team got a new head coach this year.

Packers Have Multiple Former Draft Picks Signed With New Teams

The Packers have found a lot of gems on day three of the NFL Draft in recent years. Some are still with the team, but Runyan is one of a few that have moved on. Green Bay drafted Elgton Jenkins in 2019, and he will start for the Cleveland Browns this year.

They drafted Cole Van Lanen in the sixth round in 2021, and he will start for the Jaguars . Josh Myers was from the same draft but went in the second round two. He will play for the New York Jets this year.

Sean Rhyan and Zack Bako-Bewele were drafted in 2022, and they will start for Green Bay. However, Rasheed Walker will start for the Carolina Panthers after being taken in the seventh round.

Jacob Monk was a fifth-round pick in 2024 and is competing to start at right guard. Jordan Morgan was a first-round pick and will start at left tackle. Lastly, John Williams and Anthony Belton were drafted in 2025. Both are competing at the swing tackle spot.

So, Green Bay clearly has a plan to draft, develop, and let linemen walk in free agency. They get supplemental picks in return and use those picks to draft more offensive linemen. Runyan Jr. is one of the bigger hits given his draft position.

articles.title: Strong Second Half Fuels Notre Dame In Season Opening Win Over Wisconsin
articles.summary: After a sluggish first half, CJ Carr and the Notre Dame offense came to life in Saturday night's season opening win over the Wisconsin Badgers at Lambeau Fie...
articles.body:
Green Bay, Wis. - It took Notre Dame a little while to get going in Saturday night's long-awaited season opener. But the Fighting Irish finally found their groove in the second half to put away Wisconsin 41-13 at historic Lambeau Field.

After a pedestrian first half that saw the Irish gain just 135 yards, they combined to gain 145 yards on their first two drives that each ended in touchdowns. Aneyas Williams ran for just 18 yards in the first half but finished with 90 yards on 20 carries. Meanwhile, CJ Carr was solid but not spectacular, going 19 of 29 for 239 yards and two touchdowns through the air to help the Irish open the season.

Notre Dame's defense gave up just 284 yards of offense to the Badgers. Wisconsin quarterback Colton Joseph , who ran for over 1,000 yards at Old Dominion last year, was held to three yards on 12 carries while passing for 217 yards.

Notre Dame's defense forced a 3-and-out to start the game, but the Irish offense was out it three plays of its own on its first possession. Carr was sacked by Sebastian Cheek on 3rd down and Jasper Scaife 's first career punt was blocked, giving the Badgers the ball at the Irish 37. Wisconsin would settle for a 27-yard field goal from Gavin Lahm for the game's first points.

The Irish offense came back with quick passes from Carr along with a handful of short runs by Williams. They drove to the Badger 34 before Spencer Porath booted a 52-yard field goal to tie the game 3-3.

Wisconsin return man Darrion Dupree muffed the ensuing kickoff and Kahanu Kia recovered at the Badger 13. Carr hit Green Bay native James Flanigan with a 3-yard touchdown pass four plays later to put the Irish on top 10-3.

Another Badger 3-and-out was softened by a booming 70-yard punt by Sean West that trickled out of bounds just in front of the end zone pylon, pinning the Irish at their own 1. Scaife punted cleanly from the back of the Irish end zone, giving Wisconsin the ball at the Irish 48.

After a personal foul on Armel Mukam moved the ball to the Irish 28, Joseph hit a wide open Malichi Coleman in the end zone to tie the game. Irish cornerback Jayden Sanders , who had a pair of pass breakups on Wisconsin's previous possession, bit on a double move by Coleman and couldn't recover. The touchdown tied the game at 10-10.

Fueled by consecutive pass plays of 18 and 30 yards to Gilbert and Faison, respectively, the Irish drove to the Badger 8 before settling for a 26-yard field goal from Porath go back up 13-10.

After being outgained 143-135 in total yards in the first half and leading by just a field goal, the Irish started the second half with the ball and marched 70 yards in nine plays en-route to a 3-yard Williams touchdown run to go up 20-10.

Wisconsin moved the ball near midfield on its ensuing drive, but DJ McKinney , an offseason transfer from Colorado, snagged an errant pass from Joseph and sailed to the endzone untouched for a 55-yard touchdown return that put the Irish up 27-10.

Moments before McKinney's pick-6, Notre Dame announced that safety Brauntae Johnson and defensive tackle Jason Onye would be out for the rest of the night's game. Irish head coach Marcus Freeman did not update their statuses after the game.

The Badgers followed that with a 36-yard field goal. The used 8:38 on the clock to drive 47 yards on 14 plays during the drive. Notre Dame followed with an 8-play, 75-yard touchdown drive, capped by a second Williams TD run from five yards out to make it a 34-13 lead with 10:48 remaining.

Fellow Irish running back Nolan James capped the night's scoring with a 28-yard touchdown catch. It marked the first TD of the sophomore running back's career.

articles.title: Trump Doonbeg to host Irish Open as Rory McIlroy prepares to defend
articles.summary: BBC Sport looks ahead to the Irish Open with Rory McIlroy trying to defend the title and President Trump poised to attend.
articles.body:
With the dust settling on Great Britain and Ireland's dramatic Walker Cup win at Lahinch, the action shifts 16 miles further down the west coast of Ireland as a quality field descends on Doonbeg for the 2026 Irish Open.

Twelve months ago, The K Club staged an Irish Open for the ages as home favourite Rory McIlroy captured his second title in dramatic fashion.

The six-time major winner again headlines a stellar field as Trump International Golf Links & Hotel in County Clare hosts the tournament for the first time.

The Irish Open precedes the tour's flagship event, the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth, which will be played next week.

With several star names in action and no shortage of storylines to follow throughout the week, here is everything you need to know about the Irish Open.

A lot. Five months after completing the career Grand Slam with a memorable win at the Masters, McIlroy sealed an emotional win in front of an ecstatic Irish crowd by beating Joakim Lagergren in a play-off.

Trailing Lagergren by two shots on the 72nd hole, McIlroy sunk a 25-foot eagle putt to take the Swede to a play-off and eventually prevailed on the third extra hole.

It was a gripping final round as McIlroy tussled for the trophy with Lagergren, overnight leader Adrien Saddier, Angel Hidalgo and Rafael Cabrera-Bello, who catapulted into contention with an ace at the third.

The win - which came nine years after his first Irish Open title - provided a well-timed boost for McIlroy just three weeks before he helped Europe retain the Ryder Cup with victory over the United States at Bethpage Black in New York.

While McIlroy will attract much of the attention in Doonbeg, he must fend off a high-quality field if he is to join European legends Seve Ballesteros, Nick Faldo, Bernhard Langer and Colin Montgomerie on three Irish Open wins.

As always, there is a strong Irish contingent. Shane Lowry, who memorably won his national title as an amateur in 2009, is chasing his first individual win in four years. The 2019 Open champion finished tied 15th last year.

Tom McKibbin arrives in decent form. The 23-year-old was in contention for last month's British Masters before a triple bogey early in the final round meant he had to settle for tied sixth.

Three-time major champion Padraig Harrington and two-time PGA Tour winner Seamus Power add further Irish interest.

Beyond the home hopes, there are a host of notable names. Two-time major winner Jon Rahm joins McIlroy in chasing a third Irish Open win after successes at Portstewart in 2017 and Lahinch two years later.

The Spaniard tees it up in Ireland amid ongoing uncertainty around LIV Golf's future. The breakaway tour, which launched in 2022, ended its season early following the withdrawal of the Public Investment Fund's financial backing.

McKibbin, England's Tyrrell Hatton and Chile's Joaquin Niemann are among the other LIV players in Ireland this week.

In addition, there is a strong European Ryder Cup flavour in the form of captain Luke Donald, Robert MacIntyre, Sepp Straka and twins Nicolai and Rasmus Hojgaard, who pipped McIlroy to the 2024 Irish Open at Royal County Down.

Five-time major winner Brooks Koepka also returns after missing the cut on his Irish Open debut last year.

US President Donald Trump - who owns the Doonbeg venue - is expected to attend the Irish Open.

Trump will be in Ireland this week as part of a two-day visit during which he will meet Irish President Catherine Connolly and hold a bilateral meeting with the Taoiseach [Irish prime minister] Micheal Martin.

He is expected to arrive in Ireland on Saturday and may present the Irish Open winner with the trophy on Sunday evening.

Donald Trump to meet Irish president on two day visit

The tee times will be released on Tuesday.

The Irish Open was first staged in 1927 and this week is the 71st edition of the event.

The tournament has been played at 21 courses across the island of Ireland, including renowned links venues Royal Portrush, Royal County Down and Portmarnock, which has hosted the tournament a record 19 times.

The cream of European talent competed during the 1980s and 1990s particularly.

Former winners include McIlroy, Rahm, Padraig Harrington, Sergio Garcia, Jose Maria Olazabal, Montgomerie, Faldo, Ian Woosnam, Ballesteros, Sam Torrance and Ben Crenshaw.

Formerly known simply as Doonbeg, the links course was designed by former world number one Greg Norman and opened in 2002.

It was redesigned by architect Martin Hawtree before the property was acquired by Trump in 2014 and renamed.

Unusually for a tour course, the layout boasts five par-fives and five par-threes. The signature hole is the par-three 14th, which can play as short as 111 yards.

articles.title: Former PGA Tour star Hunter Mahan hints at future run on senior circuit, stepping into posting golf content
articles.summary: Hunter Mahan reveals his wife sparked him to post golf content after years away, and now a PGA Tour Champions bid could be next when he turns 50.
articles.body: Hunter Mahan walked away from the PGA Tour in 2021 and has been open about being completely burnt out on all things involved with the non-stop grind of professional golf. Over the last five years, he's enjoyed the dad life at home, started to coach high school golf, and recently got the itch to pick up the clubs again, albeit in a different capacity. Mahan, a six-time winner on the PGA Tour, jumped into the golf content space in June and has been posting videos of his own journey back into the game, instructional videos, and anything in between while growing his Instagram following to over 55,000. "My wife just took some videos, and she said, 'You should start playing a little bit more, I can tell you're interested,'" Mahan recalled in an interview with OutKick. "So, I went out to the course the next day and hit record on that first video, and just sort of talked about it, and I wasn't sure how it looks or how it feels, but this is kind of what I'm thinking about doing. The response from all the people, my fans I guess, if you want to call them that, was so positive. It was sort of overwhelming, and we were sort of surprised by it." YOUTUBE GOLFER GRANT HORVAT IS SELLING KIDS GOLF CLUBS WITH AN ALARMINGLY HIGH PRICE TAG While Mahan is enjoying the new endeavor in the golf content space, he also shared that potentially competing on the PGA Tour Champions is on the table as well. He has a little over five years until he turns 50 and becomes eligible to compete on the senior circuit, but the competitive juices appear to be returning as he's already eyeing a potential return to professional competition. "I am exploring all things right now, and trying to figure all that out, and trying to figure out what can my place be in golf today," Mahan continued. "I've got over five years until the senior tour and see if I want to do that, the Champions Tour, and that could be a lot of fun because I've got so many friends that I played golf with that we're all going to turn 50 around the same time, so that could be a lot lof of fun. articles.title: Solheim Cup: Mimi Rhodes ready to fulfil childhood dream for Team Europe and backs Anna Nordqvist's side for home win
articles.summary: Team Europe look to regain Solheim Cup from Team USA at Bernardus Golf this week; Mimi Rhodes one of four rookies in Anna Nordqvist's side chasing home win in the Netherlands; watch the opening day live on Friday from 6am on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
Rhodes makes her Solheim Cup debut for Team Europe this week at Bernardus Golf, having been named among Nordqvist's captain's picks last month, where the hosts look to regain the trophy after their 2024 defeat to Team USA.

The Englishwoman enjoyed a strong amateur career before claiming three wins during her Ladies European Tour rookie season last year, with Rhodes now looking to build on her maiden LPGA Tour campaign by achieving a lifelong goal of representing Europe.

"For me, it's what I've been working for the last 12 years since I started playing," Rhodes exclusively told Sky Sports .

"You have it on the TV and it's what you'd wait two years to watch. I have so many vivid memories of watching on TV at my grandparents' house and with my family - we're all into team sport and we love watching team golf.

"It's just such a huge week that everyone has to wait for every two years, so it's so hard to put into words that I'm actually going to be playing in it.

"This has literally been the No 1 thing that I've dreamt of since I turned pro, even more than winning majors or anything. I've just wanted to represent Europe."

Rhodes started the year with back-to-back top-10 finishes but later feared she may not get a captain's pick, having missed seven cuts in an eight-tournament stretch from April to July before a solid finish to the qualification campaign.

She made the cut at the ISPS Handa Women's Scottish Open and AIG Women's Open, as many of her qualification rivals failed to impress, with Rhodes only finding out about her spot when Nordqvist called her after the final women's major of the year.

"That phone call was just so surreal," Rhodes admitted. "When you want something this badly and then it suddenly happens, it's like, 'wow, is this actually real?'

"It was such a stressful couple of months. I just didn't know what to expect, honestly, when I got the call. I was fearing the worst and had come to terms with it a bit!

"I would have been devastated to miss out but I was just so happy that that she picked me. I just want to make her [Nordqvist] proud and I just can't wait to play."

Rhodes was involved in the PING Junior Solheim Cup at Gleneagles in 2019, before watching from inside the ropes as Suzann Pettersen snatched a dramatic 14.5-13.5 victory for Europe.

"That was a pretty cool memory," Rhodes added. "They had a little party and we got invited in, so that was incredible.

"Watching it inside the ropes, I was thinking to myself, 'I want to work hard to get playing on that team and representing Europe'. I think it's the greatest achievement in women's golf to represent your continent."

The last three Solheim Cups held in Europe have produced the three closest finishes in its history, as 2015 and 2019 were both won by a single point ahead of the 2023 contest finishing 14-14, while Rhodes is confident Europe can come out on top and regain the trophy.

"I think on paper, it doesn't really matter how strong their team [USA] is compared to ours," Rhodes insisted. "I could tell at the practice there were a lot of good vibes, and we're going to have a lot of fun, so I think it's going to intimidate the other team."

"Anna's going to be an amazing captain - I got that vibe from her at the practise. She's a really great leader, so I think she's going to steer us in the right direction and bring the vibes.

"I think she's going to be proud of us regardless, which relaxes us a bit, but she'll have us in check! She's really good with her words, and we're looking forward to looking up to her as our captain."

"We're going to make her proud and bring it home."

Deshaun Watson will be starting at quarterback for the Browns in Week 1, but head coach Todd Monken left the door open to the possibility that another quarterback could also see playing time against the Jaguars.

Rookie Taylen Green made the 53-man roster and Monken was asked at a Monday press conference if the team could possibly have a package of plays in the playbook to take advantage of the sixth-round pick's athleticism.

"There could be a package where we have him," Monken said.

Monken went on to stress that it is a possibility rather than something the team is actively planning to have in place and that "three's a lot" when asked about having Green active alongside Watson and backup Shedeur Sanders. The Jaguars probably won't be losing much sleep about that possibility, but it will be something to watch out for if Green avoids the inactive list on Sunday afternoon.

articles.title: Solheim Cup 2026: All you need to know as Europe host US at Bernardus Golf
articles.summary: All you need to know as Europe gets ready to host the United States in the 20th edition of the Solheim Cup at Bernardus Golf in the Netherlands.
articles.body:
The 20th edition of the Solheim Cup takes place between 11-13 September as Europe host the United States at Bernardus Golf in the Netherlands.

Europe are looking to regain the trophy after losing 15½-12½ in Virginia two years ago in the biggest team competition in women's golf.

BBC Sport will have live radio commentary on 5 Live Sports Extra 3 across all three days - which is now also available via most smart speakers - and daily highlights on television.

There will also be live text commentary, video highlights, reaction and analysis on the BBC Sport website and mobile app.

The Solheim Cup is a biennial match that is played over three days, between two teams of 12 women from Europe and the United States.

It is named in honour of the Norwegian-American golf club manufacturer Karsten Solheim and his wife Louise, who have sponsored the event since its inaugural contest in 1990, and have also played a huge part in supporting the women's game over the past 50 years.

The US have won the trophy 11 times, Europe have won seven and there has been one tie - the dramatic 14-14 draw at Finca Cortesin in Spain in 2023.

Who will captain Europe & the United States?

Both teams are under new leadership, with Anna Nordqvist captaining Europe and Angela Stanford, who has served as an assistant captain three times, taking the helm for the United States.

Three-time major champion Nordqvist, who announced her retirement as a player in August, will be assisted by fellow Swede Caroline Hedwall and Dutch golfer Anne van Dam.

Mel Reid also be part of Nordqvist's staff after previously taking on a similar role for Catriona Matthew in 2019 at Gleneagles and Suzann Pettersen at the Robert Trent Jones Golf Club, two years ago.

Kristy McPherson, Paula Creamer and Brittany Lang, who all played in the 2009 edition with Stanford, make up the backroom team for the United States.

With English pair Lottie Woad and Charley Hull in their ranks Europe go into the contest boasting more players inside the top 10 in the world than their opponents.

Woad and Hull were among the eight automatic qualifiers for Europe's team.

They are joined by France's Celine Boutier, Carlota Ciganda of Spain, Germany's Esther Henseleit and Swedish duo Maja Stark and Linn Grant and Denmark's Nanna Koerstz Madsen.

Ireland's Leona Maguire, Spain's Julia Lopez Ramirez, France's Nastasia Nadaud and England's Mimi Rhodes compete the line-up for Europe.

In Nelly Korda, the United States can field the current world number one, who has won two major championships this season.

Korda, who triumphed at the Chevron Championship in April and the US Women's Open in June, was an automatic qualifier for the 12-strong team alongside Angel Yin, Jennifer Kupcho, Yealimi Noh, Auston Kim, Lauren Coughlin and Allisen Corpuz.

Andrea Lee and Alison Lee will also feature for the US by virtue of their places in the world rankings, while Stanford named Megan Khang, Rose Zhang and Lindy Duncan as her captain's picks.

What's the Solheim Cup format and scoring?

There will be 28 matchplay matches over three days in foursomes, fourballs and singles. Each match is worth one point with half a point awarded to both teams if they are tied.

The team who gets to 14½ points first wins the Solheim Cup outright. As current holders, the US will retain the trophy if the contest was to end in a 14-14 draw.

Foursomes - there are four matches, played in pairs, on Friday and Saturday. Each pair uses one ball hitting alternate shots with the lowest score on each hole winning.

Fourballs - there are four matches, played in pairs, on Friday and Saturday. All four players use their own ball The lowest scoring ball on each hole from each side is taken.

On Sunday all 24 players from both teams compete in 12 singles matches.

Temperatures will peak at around 21C over the three days of competition on the heathland course that only opened in 2018.

However, there is also a strong likelihood of showers and breezy conditions which will provide an added layer of difficulty on a course that demands precision.

Bernardus Golf hosted the DP World Tour's KLM Open between 2021-2023.

How to follow the Solheim Cup on the BBC

19:30-20:00 BST: Solheim Cup preview programme on BBC Radio 5 Live

06:30-17:00: Live text commentary on BBC Sport website and app, with updates on BBC Radio 5 Live

13:00: Live radio commentary on BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra 3 and BBC Sport website and app

10:00-close of play: Live text commentary on BBC Sport website and app

11:00-close of play: Live radio commentary on BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra 3 and BBC Sport website and app

You can also follow live and uninterrupted on most smart speakers.

On Friday, just tell your device to 'ask BBC Sounds to play Solheim Cup - day one'. For Saturday's coverage, you'll need to ask for 'day two', and on Sunday ask for 'day three'.
